aboutH2: Into Action Recovery 100 Ave: Residential Addiction Program in North Surrey
intro: Into Action Recovery 100 Ave is one of Into Action's three Surrey houses for men in early recovery. It sits on 100 Avenue in north Surrey, close to the city centre, and runs the First Stage program: a structured live-in stay of about 60 days built around groups, counselling and the Twelve Steps.

It is a smaller listing than Bear Creek, with fewer reviews online, but the routine is the same one Into Action has used since 2012. Men share the house and the meals, and staff lead the day from an early check-in to an evening meeting.

pillars.title: From Morning Check-In to the Evening Meeting
pillars.body: Into Action fills the day at 100 Ave on purpose. After the morning check-in there is individual counselling, then group therapy, then a block of physical fitness. Shared meals break up the afternoon, and the evening closes with a recovery meeting, often out in the community with the rest of the house. Recovery assignments fill the gaps.

pillars.title: Plain Bedrooms, Shared House
pillars.body: The bedrooms Into Action has photographed at 100 Ave are simple: wood furniture, a lamp, a fan, and either one bed or two. Snacks are always out, and residents can bring their own food and protein powder and keep them in a labelled resident fridge or a dry-goods shelf. Smoking is allowed only in a designated spot outside.

pillars.title: Staff Who Have Done It Themselves
pillars.body: Many of Into Action's group facilitators and support workers went through the program before they worked there, and their bios on the centre's website say so plainly. Group sessions are led by facilitators with social service, coaching and addiction counselling training, and the Program Manager holds CCAC and ICADC certification. For a man who has tried treatment before, that lived experience is often the reason he gives Into Action a try.

overviewH2: Into Action Recovery 100 Ave: Centre Overview
overview: 100 Ave is for adult men who need to be out of their usual surroundings to stop drinking or using, especially men who have relapsed after outpatient help. It treats addiction only. Withdrawal, psychiatric care and prescriptions are handled outside the house, through a partnered virtual clinic or a resident's own doctor.

location.heading: Into Action Recovery 100 Ave in Surrey, British Columbia

faqIntro: Answers come from Into Action's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: What does a day look like at Into Action Recovery 100 Ave?
faqs.a: It runs to a set schedule from morning to evening. Men begin with a check-in, then attend one-to-one counselling, group therapy and physical fitness, and end the day at a recovery meeting. Downtime is kept short on purpose, because Into Action says idle hours are when cravings take over.

faqs.q: How much does the 100 Ave house cost?
faqs.a: recovery.com estimates $10,000 to $30,000 CAD, depending on length of stay. Into Action is private pay and gives a full breakdown on the first call rather than publishing prices online.

faqs.q: How long do men stay at 100 Ave?
faqs.a: Usually 60 days or longer. Into Action's First Stage has a 60-day minimum with extensions, its other pages mention 30, 60 and 90-day options, and recovery.com lists 30 to 90 days. Into Action says most men do better with 60 days or more.

faqs.q: Do I need to detox before coming to 100 Ave?
faqs.a: Yes, if you need medical withdrawal management. The house has no medical staff, so detox happens at another facility first. Into Action's intake team says it can help book detox so you move straight into the house afterwards.

It is at 12991 100 Avenue in north Surrey, a few minutes by car from Surrey Central and the city centre around King George Boulevard. Downtown Vancouver is roughly 35 minutes away over the Pattullo Bridge, and New Westminster and Burnaby are 15 to 25 minutes away.

faqs.q: What therapies are used at 100 Ave?
faqs.a: Group therapy and one-to-one counselling are the core. recovery.com lists CBT, DBT, trauma-focused therapy, relapse prevention and 12-step facilitation for the Surrey houses, and Into Action's own FAQ adds SMART Recovery and wellness groups.

faqs.q: Does 100 Ave treat anxiety or depression?
faqs.a: Not directly. Into Action says it is not a mental health facility and focuses on stopping substance use. It supports whatever mental health plan a resident already has with his own care team, including medication.

faqs.q: How do families stay in touch?
faqs.a: Contact starts after the first restriction period and goes as far as the resident wants. Into Action encourages family involvement, and once restrictions lift a resident can ask for a weekend pass.

faqs.q: Is 100 Ave the same as Into Action's other Surrey houses?
faqs.a: The program is the same. Into Action says all three Surrey houses run the same treatment model; they differ in the building and the neighbourhood. The other two are on 87B Avenue in Newton (Bear Creek) and on 113B Avenue.
